title: DDIA 1 · TRADE-OFFS IN DATA SYSTEMS ARCHITECTURE
subtitle: No perfect systems, only trade-offs: operational or analytical, source or derived, cloud or self-hosted, one node or many.
footer: Study notes on Designing Data-Intensive Applications, 2nd edition (Kleppmann & Riccomini). Read the book.

blocks.text: Apps hit OLTP databases (few rows, by key, ms). Reports scan history in a warehouse fed by ETL/ELT, so they never slow the site.

panels.label: SYSTEM OF RECORD VS DERIVED DATA

items: System of record: the authoritative copy; each fact written there first
Derived: caches, search indexes, views, warehouse tables, ML models
Lose a derived dataset? Rebuild it from the source

blocks.text: When copies disagree, the system of record wins.
Data lives in replicated object storage; query nodes keep only a cache, so compute scales in minutes and is paid for separately.

items: Fault tolerance and availability
Data or load beyond one machine
Latency for users worldwide
Elasticity, specialised hardware
Legal data residency

blocks.text: Price: partial failure, consistency, tracing. If one node will do, use one node.

items: GDPR right to erasure vs immutable logs and backups
Crypto-shredding: per-user keys, delete the key
Data minimisation: collect and keep only what you need
Microservices: a technical fix for a people problem
"Where do dashboards read from?"
Not the OLTP DB. CDC/ETL into a warehouse or lakehouse with column storage.
"Which store is the source of truth?"
One system of record per fact; caches and indexes are derived and rebuildable.
"Managed or self-hosted?"
Managed for small teams and spiky load; self-host when load is big and steady or control matters.
"User asks to be deleted?"
Delete everywhere derived data went; crypto-shred immutable logs and backups.
